key_insight: Agglomeration-based multigrid preconditioners remove the need for conforming coarse meshes while retaining provable condition-number bounds for conforming finite element systems.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports iterative finite element solvers on complex domains without requiring a conforming mesh hierarchy.
method: Precondition fine-mesh conforming Lagrange elements using coarse polytopal DG or hybrid high-order discretisations.
Build all coarse levels by mesh agglomeration and connect them with geometric multigrid.
Transfer coarse solutions by element-wise interpolation and nodal averaging, with local potential reconstruction for the hybrid high-order variant.
evidence_signal: Experiments in 2D and 3D on structured and unstructured meshes with automatically clustered agglomerates confirm preconditioner robustness.
watch_item: The proved condition-number bounds grow as O((H/h)^3), or O((H/h)^2) for DG with suitably scaled penalties, so aggressive coarsening can affect solver performance.
paper_title: Geometric Multigrid Preconditioners for conforming Finite Element Methods on Arbitrarily Agglomerated Meshes
